messages:
maria: ALERT from prometheus -> multiple serving pods in gpu-pool-2 reporting CUDA illegal memory access + OOM (containers exiting). stacktraces show misaligned address in kernel. Rolling incident.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-214 - Severity: P1. Pager: ryan-oncall. Runbook: /runbooks/cuda-illegal-access
ryan-oncall: I'm on it. Can someone confirm impacted customers and if we have automated fallback? :eyes:
sam-infra: seeing ~12 pods crashed across nodes gpu-02,gpu-03,gpu-07. Node oom_kill logs show "illegal memory access" before OOM. Suspect kernel pagewalk race.
olivia-eng-runtime: grabbing logs and heap traces. Early look: same stacktrace across pods, kernel addresses misaligned during pagewalks. Likely NV driver + kernel interaction or recent kernel update on nodes.
maria: rolling node list -> gpu-02,03,07. Started cordon/drain on gpu-03 to reduce customer impact. Notifying customers via CS.
karim-cs: Prepping customer message for a few affected tenants (batch inference jobs failing). ETA for update 20m.
olivia-eng-runtime: quick mitigation: disable container-level shared page cache (TEMP) and force restart runtime for affected pods. Command:
```
kubectl delete pod -l pool=gpu-2 -n serving --grace-period=0 --force
kubectl annotate node gpu-02 workload-isolation=true
```
Note: this forces cold KV-cache warmups, might increase latency.
ryan-oncall: applied restarts on gpu-03 and gpu-07. Watchdog: nodes still report occasional illegal memory access events but crash rate dropped from 15/min to ~2/min.
sam-infra: opened ALT-VMs in same AZ, provisioning hot spares. If nodes continue flapping we will migrate workloads to dedicated spare pool.
olivia-eng-runtime: proposing hotpatch: pin lmod kernel module to fallback branch (workaround for misaligned pagewalk path). Patch tested in staging with no regressions. Need approval to roll to 3 nodes.
jay-sre-lead: Approve hotpatch to gpu-02/03/07 as canary with heavy monitoring. Coordinate with infra to limit to 1 node at a time. Tagging @security for driver interaction review.
security-bot: Quick scan: no sensitive data exposure observed in logs; driver interaction non-privileged. OK to proceed with hotpatch under monitoring.
ryan-oncall: rolling hotpatch to gpu-03 now. Will monitor errors and customer rate.
incident-bot: HOTPATCH DEPLOY STARTED by ryan-oncall -> INC-2026-214 -> change-id: chg-7890
olivia-eng-runtime: after hotpatch gpu-03 error rate down to 0.4/min and no new OOMs for 12m. gpu-02 still noisy.
karim-cs: Sent update to customers: 'We are mitigating a GPU runtime issue; some jobs may be delayed ~30-60m. We'll follow up when stable.'
ryan-oncall: migrating critical tenant workloads off gpu-02 to patched gpu-03 and spares. Rolling restarts to avoid thundering herd.
olivia-eng-runtime: remediation steps recorded in ticket INC-2026-214, incl logs + stacktraces + repro steps. Assigning postmortem to @olivia-eng-runtime.
maria: customers seem to be stable; closing active P1 window after 90m. Leaving incident open for followup and RCA. ETA postmortem in 72h.
karim-cs: customers acknowledged, one enterprise asked for root cause writeup and whether dedicated capacity would help; CS will coordinate followup.
ryan-oncall: final notes: revert any non-prod kernel tweaks, schedule kernel/driver upgrade window with infra. Thanks team :tada:
